title: Royalty Pharma Research Report
name: Royalty Pharma
tagline: Royalty Pharma is the largest buyer of biopharma royalties. It pays drug developers and universities up front for a share of future sales, so it earns from many blockbusters without running labs or sales forces. The stock went nowhere for four years after its 2020 IPO, then more than doubled from its late-2024 low.
kpis: operating costs as a share of receipts

chapters.title: The founding story
chapters.lede: Pablo Legorreta, a Mexican-born investment banker, saw that universities and small biotechs owned valuable royalty rights they couldn't easily turn into cash. In 1996 he started Royalty Pharma to buy them. For almost 30 years it was run by a separate management company that Legorreta owned, until shareholders voted in 2025 to bring management in-house.

items: Founder and CEO. He was the sole owner of the external manager until 2024 and has led the company's dealmaking since 1996.
The executives who used to work for the external manager became Royalty Pharma employees in 2025 and received about half of the equity issued in the deal.
They voted 99.9% in favor of internalizing management in May 2025, ending the external fee structure.
Legorreta founds Royalty Pharma in New York to buy royalty interests from academic institutions and biotechs, run by an external manager.
Royalty Pharma buys the Cystic Fibrosis Foundation's royalties on Vertex's CF drugs for about $3.3B. The franchise becomes a cornerstone of the portfolio.
It lists in the middle of the pandemic, one of the largest biopharma IPOs to that point.
The shares drift from the high $40s to the mid $20s as rates rise and investors question the external-manager fees and patent expirations in the portfolio.
A $500M agreement with Ionis puts $150M of value on pelacarsen royalties and $350M on Spinraza.
Shareholders approve acquiring the external manager with 99.9% of votes cast.
A large funding partnership backs daraxonrasib, a Phase 3 pancreatic-cancer drug. Royalty Pharma buys back $1.2B of its own stock.
Royalty Pharma targets at least $4.7B of portfolio receipts by 2030 and a mid-teens average annual total shareholder return.
Novartis's Lp(a) HORIZON outcomes trial misses its primary endpoint, and Royalty Pharma later takes a $150M non-cash impairment.
Q3 receipts rise 9% to $890M, and 2026 guidance goes up to $3.50–3.55B.

chapters.title: Early challenges
chapters.lede: The model is simple, but buying royalties brings its own risks: clinical failures, patent expirations and a cost of capital that moves with interest rates. Public investors added a governance complaint. Tap a card to see how each played out.

items: For decades the company paid a separate, Legorreta-owned manager, which critics said misaligned incentives.
In 2025 Royalty Pharma acquired the manager with 99.9% shareholder support. Costs are now 5.5–6% of receipts, and many investors see the change as the turning point for the stock.
Royalties are long-dated cash flows. When rates rose in 2022–23 they were worth less, and the company's own borrowing cost rose too.

The stock bottomed near $25.50 in December 2024. Since then, faster growth and buybacks have mattered more than rates. Net interest paid is still rising: $167M in Q3 2026 against $123M a year earlier.
Every royalty ends when its drug loses exclusivity, so the company must keep buying new ones just to stand still.
Royalty Pharma has kept committing billions to newer drugs, including more than $2.6B of deals in 2025 and over $1.25B in Q1 2026.
Funding drugs still in development can pay off well, or go to zero.
Pelacarsen failed in 2026. Royalty Pharma says the deal was structured to recover its capital plus a modest return, because Spinraza royalties came in the same package.
It isn't a pharma company, a biotech or a bank, so few investors own it as a natural fit.
It has turned to steady guidance raises, a growing dividend and large buybacks, retiring about 8.8% of its shares in one program.
As royalty financing became popular, private funds and credit investors began competing for deals.
Royalty Pharma's scale lets it write checks of $1–2B, and its synthetic royalties and R&D funding go beyond buying existing royalties.

chapters.title: Growth
chapters.lede: Royalty Pharma's top line is portfolio receipts: the cash it collects from royalties and milestones. Growth sped up in early 2026 on new launches and then slowed in Q3, which is the main point of debate now.

chapters.title: Stock trajectory
chapters.lede: The shares started trading in the high $40s in June 2020 and then fell for four years, bottoming near $25.50 in December 2024. Internalizing management, faster growth and buybacks then drove a re-rating to record highs. Hover over the line, switch to the S&P 500 comparison, or click an event.

events: Listed on Nasdaq in the middle of the pandemic and traded well above its IPO price on day one.
Four years of underperformance, with rates and governance worries weighing.
The Lp(a) outcomes trial misses, but the stock holds up because the deal was structured to recover its capital.
Guidance raised to $3.50–3.55B. Shares rose about 1.7%.

chapters.title: What it owns
chapters.lede: Royalty Pharma holds royalties on dozens of approved drugs, plus funding stakes in drugs still in trials. A few franchises do most of the work today, while newer launches are expected to carry growth toward 2030.

items.title: Cystic fibrosis (Vertex)
items.text: These are royalties on Vertex's CF medicines, including Trikafta, bought from the Cystic Fibrosis Foundation.
items.more: This is the biggest and most durable single franchise in the portfolio.

items.title: Tremfya (J&J)
items.text: An immunology drug whose new bowel-disease indications are driving fast royalty growth.

items.title: New launches
items.text: Management named these as the main contributors to Q3 royalty growth. Voranigo treats brain cancer, Evrysdi treats spinal muscular atrophy and Imdelltra treats lung cancer.

items.title: Development-stage bets
items.text: Royalty Pharma's largest R&D funding partnership is in pancreatic cancer, where a Phase 3 trial nearly doubled overall survival in second-line patients.
items.more: Pelacarsen showed the other side of this strategy when it failed its outcomes trial in September 2026, leading to a $150M impairment.

items.title: Q3 2026 additions
items.text: It bought royalties on Arcutis's Zoryve and Takeda's Mimrylo for about $100M each.

chapters.title: What the company prizes
chapters.lede: Royalty Pharma describes itself as funding innovation across the biopharma ecosystem. In practice, five principles show up again and again in its deals and its capital allocation. Tap one to see how each works.

blocks.label: Principle
items: Fund innovation, not just buy cash flows
Provide capital at every stage, from academic royalties to Phase 3 funding and synthetic royalties.
Deals include the Revolution Medicines partnership, J&J and Teva programs worth up to $1B, and the Ionis funding.
No single trial failure should break the company.
When pelacarsen failed, the $150M impairment was small against $3.5B of annual receipts.
Keep a small team and low overhead.
Operating and professional costs are 5.6% of receipts, with a full-year target of 5.5–6.0%.
The 2025 internalization passed with 99.9% support, and management now owns equity directly.
Buy back stock when it's cheap and grow the dividend.
It repurchased $1.2B in 2025 and raised the dividend 7% in 2026.

chapters.title: Why it's on the radar: the 13F view
chapters.lede: RPRX made the Insights tab because the number of tracked funds holding it grew from 5 to 8 in a year, four of them as conviction positions, while its total 13F footprint stays modest. It also has a full five-year track record, unlike the other two stock picks.

blocks.html: Quant money is piling in: AQR, Two Sigma and Renaissance all built up their RPRX positions through 2026. Renaissance's stake reached about $109M, or 0.15% of its book. Bridgewater opened a new position in Q2 2026.

chapters.title: Future outlook: opportunities & risks
chapters.lede: Analysts rate the stock a Buy, but the price has already run past most published targets. Bulls point to the launch pipeline and the 2030 target. Bears point to slowing royalty growth, rising interest costs and binary clinical risk.

blocks.note: MarketBeat shows an average target of about $63.29 from 9 analysts. Most named targets date from spring 2026, before the stock's latest run, so the shares now trade above the consensus.

opp: Tremfya (+61%), Voranigo, Evrysdi and Imdelltra are ramping up and underpin the target of at least $4.7B of receipts by 2030.
A Phase 3 that nearly doubled overall survival in second-line pancreatic cancer could make it one of the largest royalties in the portfolio.
Biotechs short of equity funding increasingly turn to royalty and R&D financing, where Royalty Pharma is the largest player.
Steady share count reduction and dividend growth support per-share returns.
Cheaper capital would raise the value of long-dated royalties and lower interest costs.
With costs at about 5.6% of receipts, most extra revenue turns into cash.
risk: Royalty-receipts growth fell from 14% to 9% in a quarter, and a few more slow quarters would hurt the growth story.
Pelacarsen showed that development-stage bets can fail. The impairment was $150M.
Older royalties keep expiring, so the company must keep doing deals just to replace them.
Net interest paid rose to $167M in the quarter, which limits cash-flow growth.
Medicare price negotiation lowers the sales base for some royalties.
The price has run above the average target, leaving less margin for error.

items: Growth settles in the mid-single digits as older royalties expire, more pipeline bets fail and interest costs keep rising. The stock falls back toward a bond-like valuation.
The business is solid, but after the re-rating most of the internalization benefit is already in the price.
Receipts grow about 10% a year toward the 2030 target, buybacks continue, and the stock trades roughly where it is.
New launches keep growth in double digits, and daraxonrasib is approved.
Royalty Pharma becomes the default funder for biotech, beats its 2030 target early, and is valued as a compounder rather than a royalty trust.
Shows whether the Q3 slowdown continues. A dividend raise has usually come in Q1.
An approval in pancreatic cancer would be a major new royalty.
This mostly closes out the impairment story.
New royalty and R&D funding deals
Steady deal flow is needed to replace expiring royalties.
Rates affect both royalty valuations and the company's own interest bill.

glossary: A right to a percentage of a product's sales, paid to whoever invented, licensed or funded it.
All cash Royalty Pharma collects from its royalties, milestones and other contracts. It is the company's top-line measure.
The part of portfolio receipts that comes from royalties on product sales.
A new royalty created by a deal: a drug maker sells a slice of future sales in exchange for cash now.
Capital that pays for a drug's trials in exchange for royalties or milestones if it succeeds.
A lump sum paid when a drug reaches a goal, such as approval or a sales level.
A write-down that cuts an asset's book value when its expected cash flows fall. It is non-cash.
Receipts minus operating costs and interest: the cash available for deals, dividends and buybacks.
A separate firm that runs a company for a fee. Royalty Pharma ended this arrangement in 2025.
Bringing management in-house by acquiring the external manager.
J&J's immunology drug (guselkumab), used for psoriasis and inflammatory bowel disease.
Roche's oral treatment for spinal muscular atrophy.
Servier's treatment for a type of brain tumor (IDH-mutant glioma).
Amgen's treatment for small-cell lung cancer.
Revolution Medicines' RAS-inhibitor in Phase 3 for pancreatic cancer.
Novartis and Ionis's Lp(a)-lowering heart drug. It failed its outcomes trial in 2026.
Lipoprotein(a), a genetically determined blood fat linked to heart disease.
Biogen's spinal muscular atrophy drug, licensed from Ionis.
The drop in a drug's sales when its patents expire and generics or biosimilars arrive.
A near-copy of a biologic drug, sold after the original's exclusivity ends.
The large, final trial stage before a drug is submitted for approval.
The main outcome a trial is designed to test. Missing it usually means the trial failed.
How long patients live after starting treatment. It is the gold-standard cancer trial outcome.
A trial that measures real clinical events, such as heart attacks, rather than lab markers.
Initial public offering. Royalty Pharma listed on Nasdaq in June 2020.
Share-price gain plus dividends over a period.
A company buying its own shares, which reduces the share count.
When investors start paying a higher (or lower) multiple for the same earnings.
An analyst's estimate of where the stock will trade in about 12 months.
A quarterly SEC report in which investment managers with over $100M list their US-listed long equity positions.
In this dashboard, a holding that is at least 0.05% of a fund's 13F long book.
